title: CI orchestrator: attestation envelope & safe rollforward for model bundle publish
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a CI orchestrator flow that produces a signed attestation envelope for model bundles and automates a time-bounded canary rollforward with automatic rollback on safety or perf regression. Goal: reduce manual steps between build and production profile publish, ensure cryptographically verifiable provenance, and avoid accidental noisy rollouts.
technical_notes: Design will produce an OCI-style bundle (model weights + metadata + perf profile) plus a signed envelope. Signing will use KMS-backed RSA keys for day-to-day, with optional HSM-protected key material for release branches. CI job produces artifacts, computes deterministic manifest hash, pushes to registry, then calls release-orchestrator to create a timed canary deployment. Verifier service validates signature + manifest before applying pin. Rollforward uses traffic-shift hooks with observability checks; rollback triggers pin reversion and schedule abort. We will add a 'canary-quorum' policy: require N successful perf checks and zero critical errors in X minutes. Performance checks include token-per-second, p95 latency, and quality regression thresholds against a small eval set.
acceptance_criteria: CI pipeline emits an attestation envelope (signed_manifest.json) alongside model bundle in registry
Release orchestrator can create a time-bounded canary that routes a configurable percent of traffic to the new bundle
Automatic rollback happens when perf SLO or eval quality thresholds are breached during the canary window
Audit log entry contains signer identity, manifest hash, and release window; entries are queryable from console
Manual override path exists to promote or abort the canary from console or CLI
work_log: 2025-02-12: Drafted ticket and initial proposal; aligned with PMs (Sana Rao) on safety thresholds
2025-02-18: Spike completed for deterministic manifest hashing and envelope format; PoC pushes to internal registry (gh:redwood-inference/model-bundles#42)
2025-02-24: Security review kickoff; decided to default to KMS signing and add HSM option for releases (security feedback from Leah Ortiz)
2025-02-28: Integrations added for release-orchestrator API; created canary policy schema and unit tests
2025-03-03: First end-to-end test: signed bundle created and canary started in staging. Observability hooks sent metrics to console pipeline. Found flaky metric aggregation — filed followup ENG-87612
notes_for_reviewers: Key trade-offs: we prioritize deterministic manifests to enable reproducible provenance at the cost of stricter build hermeticity. If build caching causes non-determinism, we'll opt to canonicalize dependency timestamps. We chose KMS-first to keep CI pipeline simple; add HSM for milestone releases. Need ops automation to rotate signer principals and retire old pins.
